channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: Wellroot opens 2 new behavioral health clinics in Georgia as 'vaccine' against mental illness
item.description: The centers in Tucker and Gainesville also provide psychiatric care, counseling and teach clients life skills.

item.title: Georgia Today: GOP Ponzi scheme fine; Moratorium on data centers; Colin Gray defense
item.description: On the Feb 27th Edition: Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger has issued a half-million-dollar fine for the multi-million-dollar Ponzi scheme that touched the top ranks of GOP politics here in Georgia; One Northeast Georgia county has approved a moratorium on new detention centers and data centers; And Colin Gray, the father of the accused Apalachee High School shooter, took the stand in his own defense this morning.

item.title: A new film follows Paul McCartney's 2nd act after The Beatles' breakup
item.description: While previous documentaries captured the frenzy of Beatlemania, Man on the Run focuses on McCartney in the years between the band's breakup and John Lennon's death.

item.title: NASA redirects Artemis moon mission program, postponing a planned astronaut landing
item.description: In shaking up its Artemis lunar program, NASA's new moon plan looks more like the Apollo missions of the 1960s. Instead of landing on the surface on Artemis III, NASA hopes to do so on Artemis IV.

item.title: GPB evening headlines for February 27, 2026
item.description: Colin Gray, the father of accused Apalachee High School shooter Colt Gray, took the stand in his own defense today; Northeast Georgia's Hall County OK a 180-day moratorium on new detention centers; appeals court dismisses water wars between Georgia, Florida and Alabama.

item.title: Pentagon puts Scouts 'on notice' over DEI and girl-centered policies
item.description: After threatening to sever ties with the organization formerly known as the Boy Scouts, Defense Secretary Hegseth announced a 6-month reprieve

item.title: How the federal government is painting immigrants as criminals on social media
item.description: Experts say this kind of media campaign is unprecedented and paints a distorted picture of immigrants and crime

item.title: OpenAI announces Pentagon deal after Trump bans Anthropic
item.description: Shortly after the president's ban of artificial intelligence company Anthropic, rival OpenAI announced it had done a deal with the Defense Department to provide its technology for classified networks.

item.title: Bill Clinton says he 'did nothing wrong' with Epstein as he faced grilling over their relationship
item.description: Former President Bill Clinton told members of Congress on Friday that he "did nothing wrong" in his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and saw no signs of Epstein's sexual abuse as he faced hours of grilling from lawmakers over his connections to the disgraced financier from more than two decades ago.

item.title: Trump says he is 'not happy' with the Iran nuclear talks but indicates he'll give them more time
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday he's "not happy" with the latest talks over Iran's nuclear program but indicated he would give negotiators more time to reach a deal to avert another war in the Middle East.
